title: How to set up evolving rep ranges (practical aspects)
summary: NH gives two concrete evolving rep range schemes from his own training: 2-5 reps over 1-3 sets for deadlifts and overhead press (high intensity), and 4-8 reps over 1-3 sets for squat and bench (more volume, lower intensity). He explains how sets stack week to week, how to spot and repeat the peak-tonnage week, and why you must never regress with this method.

claims.claim: NH prefers giving keys of understanding rather than precooked programs; there are many ways to make evolving rep ranges work, including ones he hasn't found.
Evolving rep range A (high intensity): 2-5 reps, 1-3 sets. Week 1: 2; week 2: 3; week 3: 3,2; week 4: 4,3,2; week 5: 5,4,3. Each week adds a rep and a new set stacks underneath.
Rest about 3-4 minutes between heavy sets in the low-rep evolving scheme.
On low-volume weeks of a low-rep scheme (e.g. just 2 heavy reps), you must find complementary volume elsewhere in the session; the 5-4-3 week is already a lot of volume, especially on deadlifts.
NH uses the 2-5 rep scheme on deadlifts and overhead press because they benefit from high intensity and stay safe for him at that percentage.
You can apply evolving rep ranges to any lift, but the more tonnage a lift moves relative to the body part moving it, the more cautious you must be with high-intensity schemes.

Evolving rep range B (more volume): 4-8 reps, 1-3 sets, used on squat and bench because NH's form breaks down on those lifts at high intensity and they stop targeting the intended muscles. Progression: 4; 5,4; 6,5,4; 7,6,5; 8,7,6 (approx.).
Choose the evolving rep range per lift based on how its form holds up: lifts whose form breaks down with heavy loads should get a higher-rep, lower-intensity scheme from the start.
Identify the hardest session in an evolving rep range, the biggest jump in tonnage (e.g. going from 5,4 to 6,5,4), and make sure the preceding days don't deplete you so you can hit it.
Don't be afraid to repeat the peak-tonnage session (e.g. redo the 6-5-4 week) to keep form clean and tonnage stable.

The whole advantage of evolving rep ranges is constant progression; if you regress, you would have been better off with a 3x5, since evolving schemes lack the skyrocketing progression of other rep schemes.
Over about a year and a half of programmed evolving rep ranges, NH missed a planned weight fewer than five times; when he plans six reps, he gets six.
NH thinks evolving rep ranges are the future of programming.
Parameters can evolve independently: you can evolve only reps with fixed sets, only sets with fixed reps, or both; all work as long as volume and intensity are manipulated.
